notes.title: The 1000xRESIST 1st Anniversary Fanzine is OUT NOW
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/f63ece85a20cd5aa04fc7bd2f22e95d5a54fd9d1.png[/img]
[h3][b][url=https://0x0ada.itch.io/blue-communion]blue communion[/url][/b], the 1000xRESIST 1st Anniversary Fanzine is [url=https://0x0ada.itch.io/blue-communion]OUT NOW[/url].[/h3]

This [b]fan-led collection[/b] features over 100 pages made by 24 contributors (and 4 mods).

Within these pages, you'll find:
[list]
[*] foreword by Remy Siu, the creative director of 1000xRESIST!
[*] fan illustrations and cosplay
[*] fan fiction, poetry, and essays
[*] micro-TTRPG and personality quiz
[*] food and drink recipes
[*] music transcription and diy craft project (standalone printable assets offered with the zine download)
[/list][h3][url=https://0x0ada.itch.io/blue-communion]Get the Fanzine here![/url][/h3]

We are so stunned by the talent and effort on display. Below is a copy of the forward, written for the fanzine. Hopefully it captures how we're feeling here at sunset visitor about this amazing display of love. This is truly next level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/052eb0bcb27049741964566d11276febafde39ac.png[/img]

[h3]Fanzine Forward[/h3]

[i]I can’t believe it’s been a year.

While working on 1000xRESIST, it felt like development would never end. There was always something left to do, some sound, animation, or piece of music. A missing voice line here, a missing texture there. A bug persisting somewhere. I’m told this is a normal feeling in game development – and certainly we had similar experiences in the arts world – but this particular timbre of endlessness was new to me. And I think, new to many of us on the team.

But... upon release, we continued to experience new things. We saw the first reviews go up. We saw players resonating with the story. We saw the first bits of fan art posted online. The first forum posts in ResetEra advocating for the game. The first messages and emails sent through our contact forms. We got to experience 1000xRESIST being discovered. Discovered by fellow devs and industry workers, discovered by the wonderful community gathering in our Discord, discovered by the amazing fans and artists online, and yes, by all the fantastic people here featured in this fanzine.

Performing arts can be lonely. Even though you perform to people in-person and in real-time, after the performance is over, you rarely see the audience again. Their engagement with the work lives inside them, in memory, and one cannot really access that. This is what I’m used to. Getting the post-performance blues.

To see fans continue to engage with 1000xRESIST, to get familiar with usernames and avatars, to answer questions on the Discord, and to witness this fanzine come together – to witness it even existing – has been remarkable. Thank you to all the contributors and organizers for making this possible. There’s so much talent and passion collected here.

We are so grateful to have this community around the game, continuing to bring new people in and spreading the word. We say that a lot. We’ll keep saying it.

1000xRESIST was by no means a guaranteed success. There was a lot of risk. A lot of challenges. After all is said and done, we still exist because of the fans. It means the world to us that they’re making these characters – this story – their own. We get to discover a whole chorus of diverse artistic voices and perspectives, and all of a sudden, it’s not so lonely anymore. It starts to feel more like a collaboration.

So, enough from me. Time to step aside and let these amazing folks take center stage! Six to one and HEKKI GRACE.

– Remy Siu (Creative Director of 1000xRESIST)
April 30th, 2025[/i]

notes.title: 1000xRESIST nominated for 2025 Hugo Awards!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/9c5c0cb53c74bd6b316c1715c425741ef35acd39.png[/img]

[h3]🚀  1000xRESIST has been nominated for a HUGO AWARD! 🚀[/h3]

This is a dream come true for us at Sunset Visitor 斜陽過客. As people who grew up reading science-fiction, we can still remember browsing the paperbacks and seeing “Hugo Award” on the front covers. We couldn’t be more excited and honoured to be nominated.

Thank you to all the fans and Worldcon members that cast a ballot for us. We greatly appreciate your support! ✨

We are doubly delighted that 1000xRESIST has secured a joint Nebula + Hugo nomination, which is something we never considered possible when we set out to make a game. We’ve been pinching ourselves for the last 48 hours.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/18bb92187bcc8f4d34c172ab5c87973adf963647.png[/img]

To celebrate, [b]Remy Siu[/b] and [b]Pinki Li[/b] take a moment to remember some influential experiences with Nebula/Hugo Award-winning books:

[h3]Pinki Li on “Left Hand of Darkness” by Ursula K. Le Guin[/h3]
[i]The Left Hand of Darkness is one of very few books I’ve read in my life that left me–upon completion—with a kind of inexplicable loss for days. Widely celebrated for its originality and revolutionarity, it offers compelling, complexing, fresh perspectives on gender, society, and otherness on an engrossing alien planet. However, what particularly stays with me, even after all these years since reading, was my embodied experience of endurance—the slow, gruelling movement of two characters amidst unforgettably punishing terrain. In all the inhospitability, The Left Hand of Darkness manages to be ingeniously funny and truly sexy. What a fantastical read in the most dreary, humanizing way. I’ve never quite been the same.
[/i]
[h3]Remy Siu on “Hyperion” by Dan Simmons[/h3]
[i]I read Hyperion when I was too young to appreciate it, but the “Priest’s Tale” is forever burned into my mind. I devoured it straight through in one sitting, delirious. The growing sense of dread and the sheer impossibility of what was unfolding – I couldn’t look away. At that young age, I never considered that science-fiction could enter such uncanny territories. I still think of the Bikura, Paul Duré, and the Tesla Tree now and again, relishing that moment of utter disbelief. What an absolute fever dream.[/i]

The Hugo Awards will be presented in a ceremony on August 16, 2025 at Seattle Worldcon 2025. Other nominated indie games include, Lorelei and the Laser Eyes, Tactical Breach Wizards, Caves of Qud, and more!

You can read more about the awards, and the other finalists here: https://seattlein2025.org/wsfs/hugo-awards/2025-hugo-award-finalists/

[h3][b]Official Wiki[/b][/h3]
If you didn’t know, 1000xRESIST now has an [url=https://1000xresist.wiki.gg/wiki/1000xRESIST_Wiki]Official Wiki[/url]. And better yet? It’s run by fans.

This Wiki wouldn’t exist without the efforts of [url=https://bsky.app/profile/mynntexts.bsky.social]Mynn[/url], Hepi Chest Cow, [url=https://bsky.app/profile/swiftcarrotcake.bsky.social]Jay[/url], [url=https://bsky.app/profile/avianaddy.bsky.social]Avi Avi[/url], [url=https://bsky.app/profile/0x0ada.bsky.social]Ada[/url], [url=https://bsky.app/profile/vitamin.games]Pidge[/url], [url=https://bsky.app/profile/cordycxps.bsky.social]fern[/url], [url=https://bsky.app/profile/spilledte.com]SpilledTe[/url] and everyone who has contributed from the Discord. Their dedication and passion to this project is inspiring to us.

If you would like to contribute, join us on our [url=https://discord.com/invite/zBMb7DH]Discord[/url]. There’s a dedicated 1000xRESIST wiki channel that’s always up to something!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/73fd852c16e1dddc6c32036040a93655c61a8e7c.png[/img]

[h3][b]Content Creators[/b][/h3]
Creators and podcasters continue to make wonderful content about 1000xRESIST. Here is just a small selection–

This [url=https://youtu.be/z945vjgY7iM?si=PFNmFyIL_ctvbOZT]Save Room[/url] video replicates the UI of the game and dives deep into personal connections. Daryl Talks Games shares their love of CH9 in [url=https://youtu.be/flQVHfDYWWk?si=i9mQGilp4zGXsKst]another video[/url]. Here is a [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uik9PjRAHpc&t]lovely essay[/url] by our Discord’s very own [url=https://bsky.app/profile/thestryderunit.bsky.social]Stryder[/url]. And WoolieVS is [url=https://youtu.be/YOaUHNulD_w?si=pW5yYFL7wDgbkmGg]streaming the game[/url] and moving through methodically! 

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5f5wjFdlDEY][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/095c7c3f0f7b9fb2886eca705ce0f3f94bbbb788.jpg[/img][/url]

We were on the [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5f5wjFdlDEY]NoClip podcast[/url]! And [url=https://youtu.be/bSK8kWoAlD0?si=5nlK1O9QzTjto0Qf]the MinnMax podcast with the Mouthwashing Devs[/url]! Remy talked about Michael Bay too much on the [url=https://youtu.be/4t12k-CrtpE?si=k9FCPxTKBjinn7j8]Storymoders Podcast[/url]. We were also featured in the [url=https://youtu.be/F9W3UDYMbpc?si=X1b8DTSwcBfLxO95]Game Maker’s Notebook Podcast[/url].

It’s been so great discovering these videos and talking to all the hosts. If you’ve finished the game and need to unpack it – check these out!

[url=https://youtu.be/bSK8kWoAlD0?si=5nlK1O9QzTjto0Qf][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/8532170aa1603fb39299d1f3a36581e432dc86e4.jpg[/img][/url]

[h3][b]GOTY Roundup[/b][/h3]
Okay.

Okay, okay. This was our first GOTY season and we were unprepared. List after list, we saw people include 1000xRESIST as one of their favourite games of 2024.

We’re going to try and name them all here, out of appreciation. A little hekki allmo for us please...

GameRant, TheGamer, Polygon, Rolling Stone, The Verge, PopMatters, Paste Magazine, NPR, NoClip, Monty Zander, Jacob Geller, Slant Magazine, Destructoid, Washington Post, Gamespot, IGN, The Short Game Podcast, Game Developer, MobileSyrup...

Hit Points, But Why Tho?, AV Club, Naughty Dog, Console Creatures, PC Gamer, Gaming In the Wild, Kotaku, Nexlander, Indieventure Podcast, Rachel Watts, New York Times, Silicon Era, Giant Bomb, PCGamesN, ScreenRant, Triple Click, SkillUp, Second Wind, Noobfeed, The Escapist..................

Remap Radio, NookGaming, Press Play Gaming, GoNintendo, Sifter, Willa Rowe, MinnMax, Video Games are Good, Maximum Fun, Player 2, ShackNews, Black Tabby Games, SideQuesting, Eurogamer, Fawzi Mesmar, Blogcritic, Swery65, GamesCreed, Gamesmatter, Metro UK, SuperJump, TouchArcade!

[b](deep breath)[/b] Whep. We think this is an incomplete list, so apologies if you mentioned 1000xRESIST on your GOTY list and we missed you!

We are just so, so grateful. We don’t know what else to say.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/76ed2ac9290ec4726377447913f5d14caaa03d3d.png[/img]

[h3][b]Awards[/b][/h3]
In the last couple of months, we’ve been nominated for some amazing awards. Here are a couple standouts!

[list]
[*] Golden Joystick – Best Storytelling
[*] New York Game Awards – Best Music, Best Writing, Best Indie, Game of the Year
[*] DICE Awards – Outstanding Achievement in Character, Story, Game Direction, Adventure Game of the Year
[*] Canadian Game Awards – Best Art Direction, Best Score/Soundtrack, Best Narrative, Best Performance, Best Audio Design, Best Debut Indie Game, Best Debut Studio, Game of the Year
[*] Debug Awards – Best Narrative, Best Voice Acting
[*] GDCA Awards – Best Narrative, Best Debut, Social Impact
[/list]
We are so excited that Nhi Do (the voice of Watcher) has been recognized in two of these nominations! She did such incredible work on the game, including being one of the very first playtesters.

We also won [b]Best International Game[/b] at SXSW Sydney and [b]Best Narrative[/b] at the inaugural [url=https://www.indiegameawards.gg/]Indie Game Awards[/url]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/60df30642008111b50f5428a88f6226ed6919ec8.png[/img]

[h3][b]Balatro[/b][/h3]
Oh, and we’re in BALA-TRO now. Thank you LocalThunk and Playstack!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/9c9c754cf71087b4b388874eae1f381acd908218.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/4856c64d8c6ceae3f15e74b2c80e681506447cc0.png[/img]

[h3][b]GOTY + Awards + Fan Passion = Sales??[/b][/h3]
The support from fans has been beyond anything we ever could have dreamed of. To everyone on socials, on Reddit, on Discord, and on ResetEra – THANK YOU. To everyone who has written about the game, covered it, asked us to be on podcasts, or recognized it in your GOTY lists – THANK YOU. Your recommendations and support have made a HUGE difference. 

It really is working – and we brought proof ;-)

As of mid-January 2025, [b]1000xRESIST has sold over 70,000 copies on all platforms![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/2300a1e8de5bc8f5a88bb085d32e771f5c66f4fd.png[/img]

That means [b]we sold 45,000 copies in the same time we sold 25,000 copies previously![/b] Most games have their biggest sales spike during launch. For us, our best sales day is now January 1st, 2025 – 7 months after launch day! This is unbelievable to us. [url=https://www.polygon.com/news/504060/1000xresist-best-sales-day-six-months-later-indie-success]Polygon even wrote about it![/url]

We can only attribute this to the great word of mouth and the passion of the fans. It was only possible because you have all been recommending the game to others. This wave of momentum started with people being upset for us about The Game Awards, then led into the GOTY lists, the Balatro Collaboration, the Autumn and Winter sale, and finally New Years. Even now, in January, our sales continue to be stronger than before!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/91e6b8e115c44821e636724939276eddd4404a85.png[/img]

(hekki holidays! We commissioned [url=https://bsky.app/profile/spilledte.com]SpilledTe[/url] to make this wonderful image)

And lastly, we passed [b]2500 Steam Reviews![/b] To everyone who has taken the time to leave something of their experience, we couldn’t be more grateful. If you haven’t left a Steam review yet, please do! It’s a great way to support indie devs!

[h3][b]What’s Next[/b][/h3]
We have a lot of things planned and we think you’ll like them.

To say carefully, we’re looking at expanding the reach of 1000xRESIST further, so keep an eye out for news and updates in the coming months.

Merch is also coming. We have started compiling a SCRIPT. Expect more Piano Books. Some more music stuffs. We are still looking at releasing models to fans, to create fan animations / content.

If you haven’t already, follow us on [url=https://bsky.app/profile/sunsetvisitor.studio]Bluesky[/url], [url=https://x.com/1000xResist]Twitter[/url], Steam, and join our [url=https://discord.com/invite/zBMb7DH]Discord[/url]. That’s where we’ll be announcing everything that we’ve been working on. We can’t wait to share it with you all this year!

[h3][b]In Closing...[/b][/h3]
The last four months have been...a lot – in the best way possible! We couldn’t be more proud of the game and so, so completely grateful for the wonderful community growing around it.

It still feels all very surreal to us, but as we get to work on new things of all kinds, we can’t help but feel we’re doing it a little less alone than the first time around.

A shoutout to the one and only [url=https://bsky.app/profile/themaarika.bsky.social]Maarika[/url], who we commissioned to do the main image for this post (and made the image below). It’s becoming tradition!

We look forward to more people discovering 1000xRESIST in 2025! We have some fun things in store.

Until next time, HEKKI GRACE.

notes.title: To You, 25,000 Copies Later
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/48a7cb78ac38c436ed7bb12972f089dd01b11c79.jpg[/img]

Hekki Allmo!

It’s been around 4 months since the release of 1000xRESIST (can’t believe) and we wanted to take a moment to update you on how it’s going and future plans.

This is going to be a somewhat long post, so settle in, grab a coffee or tea, and put your feet up on the chair; there’s lots to cover!

Before we get into it – THANK YOU. These past few months have been wild. We’re so grateful to everyone who has been spreading the word about 1000xRESIST. We honestly wouldn’t be here without you. We’re serious.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/b1ffafee6073ef9d65fb78adae7247af55a12af8.png[/img]

[h3][b]Fan Reception[/b][/h3]

We’ve been floored by the fan reception. Sometimes when you work on something for so long, you just have your head down in it. The last couple of months have been some of the most rewarding of our careers. As you may know, many of us on the team are from the experimental performing arts. The reach for that is confined to physical location. To have the game reach people across the world and make an impact has been such a privilege.

We’re so thankful to everyone who has been shouting about the game, writing essays, making videos, memes, cosplay, streaming, drawing AMAZING fan art – the burgeoning community around the game just makes us feel all the feels. We see you – on socials, on Reddit, on Discord, on ResetEra – and we appreciate you! We had a cast party in July and it was so great to show the performers all the fan art and comments. They were ecstatic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/14c943b621c4ac51694f62f1fd62566db7095900.jpg[/img]


We also recently hit the [b]1000 Steam Review milestone[/b] and it means so much to us that people are taking the time to leave something of their experience. To everyone who wrote, “if the devs ever read this...,” we do read it and some of the responses have made us tear up (in a good way!). If you haven’t left a review yet, please do! It’s one of the best ways to support us and in general, indie devs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/634a344496952c0b7bdd96a0b0a2172f2f292a36.jpg[/img]

Fan Art credits - Left to right: [url=https://www.instagram.com/yuulinshi/]Yuu@home[/url], [url=https://www.maarika.com/]Maarika[/url], [url=https://garmmy.tumblr.com/)]garmmy[/url], [url=https://linktr.ee/confettibri]Brianna Lei[/url], [url=https://bsky.app/profile/peachiegrey.bsky.social]Peach & Grey[/url], [url=https://www.instagram.com/antibioticgel/?hl=en]roll[/url], [url=https://x.com/smushypanda3]smushypanda[/url].

[h3][b]Content Creators[/b][/h3]

The videos and podcasts being created by content creators has been overwhelming. We’re still catching up on all of them! [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9bv6PDk1GdU&t=4s]Geeks + Grounds did a month-long “book club” style playthrough[/url] with multiple spoilercasts. [url=https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAIcZs9N41701WkFvOdSRWvj-ZpMBIqG4&si=QjFgpAVz11jROcBU]Welonz did a wonderful playthrough[/url], speaking from her perspective as a member of the Hong Kong diaspora. [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G74nCKVL_CY&t=1s]Matt Horton published a one-hour deep dive[/url]. And dotzip recently released [url=https://share.transistor.fm/s/9180106a]a FIVE HOUR long epic spoilercast[/url].

Don’t forget [url=https://soundcloud.com/bullet-points/episode-97-1000xresist]Bullet Points Spoilercast[/url], our interview with [url=https://youtu.be/xb8A6VgQg8I?si=4hnEiORwD_wIfDGI]Gaming In The Wild[/url] and [url=https://animesickos.com/episode/192-remy-siu-goes-guesto-mode]Anime Sickos[/url]. And of course, [b]Jacob Geller’s stunning video “[url=https://youtu.be/Wmi_6D6vwBQ?si=JCAktZ4yRkLWGHIo]Nothing Ever Stops Existing[/url].[/b]”

There’s more and I’ll be sure to list them next time – we’re amazed by all this and want to thank all the creators for taking the time to share their passion for the game.

[previewyoutube=Wmi_6D6vwBQ;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3][b]Press Reception[/b][/h3]

The press response has been truly, wonderfully, humbling. 1000xRESIST is currently sitting on OpenCritic’s 2024 Hall of Fame with heavy hitters like Hades II, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, and Animal Well. This is something we never could have dreamed of. The whole team has been taken aback time and again by the thoughtful writing in so many reviews.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/ecc624aa4961400c7fe23c67889558a0c6016057.png[/img]

Here are some (but not all) of our favourite quotes:

[i]“The feeling I experienced while playing 1000xRESIST is similar to the one I experienced while playing NieR: Automata—it’s the feeling that I’ll remember this story for the rest of my life...”[/i] [b]– Paste Magazine[/b]

[i]“1000xRESIST doesn’t just show what’s possible for narrative adventures or games in general; it shows what’s possible for art and entertainment as a whole.”[/i] [b]– GoNintendo[/b]

[i]“What a journey that was. Every time I thought I knew where it was going, it went somewhere else.”[/i] [b]– TouchArcade[/b]

[i]“1000xRESIST is unlike anything I’ve played before. Not since FromSoftware’s Dark Souls has a game captivated me utterly.”[/i] [b]– Pop Matters[/b]

[i]“It’s a cathartic and authentic representation of the common ground Asian Americans/Canadians share, extending to anyone who grew up a first generation from an immigrant family – the disconnect we feel from being pushed into assimilating and functioning in a western society while clinging on (sometimes reluctantly) to the cultures of our motherland. It's also an open invitation to those on the outside to see what our lives are really like, and a shining example of how the local is universal.”[/i] [b]– IGN[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/4f3196f13a4f61f6c459e835459b00524e52aea9.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]How It’s Going[/b][/h3]

We launched during one of the busiest days in indie game history and even through that, we were able to punch up. To date 1000xRESIST has sold over 25,000 copies! And while this number may not seem huge compared to other games shipped on that day, it’s extremely meaningful to us.

What does it mean? It means we can keep the lights on. [b]It means we can keep making games.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/6b0ea92a4de19dad24f2bb504ce8c7ee4f668e52.png[/img]

So, please excuse me for repeating: THANK YOU. To all the people who have supported the game by telling their friends, colleagues, and family – I said this above, and I really mean it, we wouldn’t be here without everything you’ve done to spread the word.

[b]It’s working.[/b] We’re seeing 1000xRESIST continue to sell well through word of mouth and we couldn’t be more excited to have more people experience this strange thing we made. We’re going to do our best to support this as much as possible going forward. For example, check out our character screenshot references for fan art ([url=https://sunsetvisitor.notion.site/1000xRESIST-Character-Screenshots-141e1464e36149239c7a79d12cd6e86c?pvs=74]1000xRESIST Character Screenshots (notion.site)[/url]).

So, six to one, sisters! Let’s continue to spread the brain rot.

[h3][b]What’s Next For 1000xRESIST[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/6ebfc13c1793d77c37010db59470d8ebb0e97100.png[/img]

First up: [b]Japanese localization![/b]

Shipping within the next three months, the game will be fully localized to Japanese. We’re really excited about this and can’t wait for Japanese audiences to experience 1000xRESIST.

We’ve also been listening to the fans on other things. We’re actively looking into making an artbook and a script. Our hope for both of these is to include cut content, in-progress pieces, and some behind the scenes nuggets. Keep an eye out – but please be a bit patient – as we want to make them worthwhile and a good insight into the process.

Fans have also expressed an interest in having access to the [b]in-game models[/b] to create fan art, fan animations, and the like. We’re also looking into this. Give us a bit of time to figure it out!

What’s more? We’re exploring [b]a physical release[/b]. Many people have expressed a desire for this, so we’re taking it seriously. We have no news to share on this just yet, but stay tuned!

[b]MERCH.[/b] Yes. We can say the first piece of merchandise coming up will be a plushie (produced by our industrious fan Pidge). We love the idea of fans making things for other fans. The pre-orders for these will be up before the end of the year!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/601198c0bdfc5b1a4ccba2a46cd10ec291515cfd.png[/img]

Let us know if you have any other merch desires in the comments or the [url=https://discord.com/invite/GZKEkuwxXH]Discord[/url]! Maybe one day, you can even have a Picture Jiao of your own...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/a64f9bf3662f613fdb6e8777538c20fe6092f77b.jpg[/img]

[b]OST IN MORE STORES.[/b] We’ve been trying to get the OST on more digital stores, but an 85-track album is a challenge to distribute digitally on major storefronts. We may need to split the OST into multiple volumes for this reason. We’re still holding off on Spotify and Apple Music streaming. Our composers get a percentage of each soundtrack sale, so in an effort to support them, we’re sticking with outright sales. For the foreseeable future, the best place to get the OST will still be Steam and Bandcamp!

[b]PIANO BOOKS.[/b] Drew has been passionate about transcribing the piano pieces in 1000xRESIST for others to play. We’ll be releasing these in small volumes, leading up to a complete book. In the meantime, check out [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8cwz85EkIy8]purpleschala’s cover of “A Teardrop.”[/url]

[b]VINYL RELEASE.[/b] We’ve heard you loud and clear. You want a record and so do the composers. We’re thinking about it. We’re working on it.

And last but not least, we’re exploring the world of [b]Film/TV adaptations.[/b] Recently CAA – one of the big talent agencies in Hollywood – approached us with a partnership to represent our IPs in that space. We’re still at the very, very early stages of this but excited to consider the possibilities, whether that be animation or live-action (our minds boggle at how that could be done).

[h3][b]What’s...N E X T[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/62a702c94888d0e51ad6ae95845774c1a31403f0.jpg[/img]

[b]We’re moving offices![/b]

We’re trading our little office with a nice view for a bigger office that looks out onto a back alley (with trees! There’s trees.)

More importantly, our new office will be [i]quieter[/i]. We do all of our voice over recordings in-house, so we’re always looking to improve the technical process. A quieter office means a lower noise floor. We’ll be able to record audio that won’t require as much cleanup in post-production (Justin will be very happy about that). With more space, we’re also hoping to record more than one performer simultaneously, so they can play off each other's energy, opening up all kinds of new opportunities.

Finally, the larger space will give our motion capture performers more room to do things without hitting a computer (or one of us).

There’s also a sink now. Thank the ALLMOTHER.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/3af45538434338d867e2a882da4fa5e4055afea8.jpg[/img]

[b]We’re making more games.[/b]

It’s both exciting and terrifying to be looking at a blank page again. It’s been awhile. We’ve been so encouraged by all your messages about future titles and I’d be lying if I said we’re not feeling the pressure.

The studio was founded to explore meaningful subject matter in new and experimental ways. Very much in the spirit of 1000xRESIST, we like left turns. All I know at this point is to expect the [i]unexpected[/i].

Come along for the ride! If it’s not clear already, we love to surprise.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/bf47a74040b6529a30443c58e680c4c7fce20855.jpg[/img]

[b]In Closing...[/b]

We’re excited to embark on this next phase, supporting 1000xRESIST and exploring new games. To risk sounding like a broken record, we’re so grateful to all the people who have supported us so far.

We’ll be sure to update everyone as things progress. notes.title: Dev Diaries: 1000xRESIST [02 - Q&A] | February update!
notes.content:
We’re back with another dev diary, where we get to update you on how and what we’re doing. This is not the graphical update dev diary that was promised in our last blog – we’re still working on that and we’ll share more soon. In its place, we’ve been sent some questions and our Creative Director, Remy Siu, and Narrative Designer, Natalie Tin Yin Gan will answer them. Let’s go! 


[b]How have dance, theatre, film, and other new media inspired and been implemented in 1000xRESIST?[/b]

[b]R:[/b] It’s hard to say, “we took this from dance, we took this from theatre, we took this from film.” A lot of it is just baked into our background and experiences working in those various mediums. When we’re not entirely sure how we want to depict a scenario or engage with the storytelling in any particular chapter, we fall back on our experiences in these different mediums where we can, like, reference works and seek ways of thinking about material that could help.

[b]N:[/b] I think Remy’s background in music composition also informs a lot aspects of the game, particularly in storytelling structure, ie. the order/duration/drama of scenes and chapters.There’s quite a bit of cute dancing in this game if you’re looking for it. It’s not capital D dance–as in traditional, formalized dance–but I think that speaks to what we value and enjoy when it comes to contemporary movement/dance aesthetics.

[b]R:[/b] There’s more joyful dancing in this than anything we’ve ever made, maybe? 

[b]N:[/b] Maybe. 

[b]R:[/b] Well, because most of the characters are oblivious to their circumstances. So they get to be happy.

[b]N:[/b] Haha, uhh not that joyful or carefree dancing is only reserved for the oblivious...

[url=https://youtu.be/MkqV2m1AZ-Q][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/33f1e96116ef8face662076cd10f8846ef7112cb.jpg[/img][/url]
[i]A scene from Devised Narratives: A 1000xRESIST Mini-Documentary[/i]


[b]What films and games did you look to as inspiration for 1000xRESIST?[/b]

[b]R:[/b] The first ones obviously on our list are NieR: Automata and the original NieR. Their playfulness with video game form and vocabulary is pretty influential to us. They showed me that there’s enough history in video games now that we can use that history, and all of the memory involved with those kinds of vocabularies, and create meaning out of it, as opposed to say, like, I don't know, the very first Doom game. Or Wolfenstein 3D, Maze War–those were maybe one of the first first-person-games ever, so there was really no history yet. So when you went into first person, it was really a novel thing. Now, there's many games we can reference like Gone Home, Tacoma, Firewatch, all of these other first person story games that didn't exist then. 

The other one is Kentucky Route Zero. Not that we have similar content, but Kentucky Route Zero doesn't care that it's a game, so to speak. Sometimes it feels like it really just wants to do what it wants to do, and lets all of the expectations about what video games should be fall to the side. And it's always changing and shifting to depict the various aspects of the story. 

I can also add one more thing: I grew up playing point and click adventure games, and those were narrative games that also didn’t 100% care about fail states. There was a real time where the fail states were not a big part of games, and would prioritize telling a story or letting you know about the characters living in that world.


[b]How much has 1000xRESIST changed over its development lifetime? Have you stuck closely to the original design idea?[/b]

[b]R:[/b] The game is way beyond anything that I originally imagined, at this point. The original demo did involve some elements, like the high school, Watcher, and the whole conceit of going back into memory and reliving this past while feeling alienated by something that is very much present day for us. In terms of how the whole thing developed in how it looks and plays, because we have the whole team on the game, it has changed a lot over the cycle of development. A lot of things like the time mechanics, the different player controllers, different viewpoints, characters, the ways the chapters unfold, that kind of stuff that I don’t think I would have been able to do by myself for various reasons, like just not knowing how. So shout out to [Senior Programmer] Colin, [Art Director] Kodai, [Producer] Natalie T, and everybody else who has contributed to making those things I just didn’t consider possible and feasible. 

[b]N:[/b] That makes me curious–is there something that was in the original concept that you had trouble letting go of from your original prototype? 

[b]R:[/b] That’s not a spoiler? Let me think. There was a time when Secretary talked only with kaomojis. I thought it was funny that you wouldn’t really get great instructions from them, like, you would still have to interpret their instructions. It was probably too much for their overall role in the game. So our compromise was that we made Secretary be voiced by a 12-year-old boy.


[b]What inspired the particular locations for the game?[/b]

[b]R:[/b] When Kodai was working on the main hub of the game, something that we would always say is that it’s transitcore, in the sense that we were really interested in these liminal public transit spaces across Asia and North America–in Vancouver, Japan, and Hong Kong. There’s a lot of Umeda Sky Building, there’s a lot of metro stations, and there’s a lot of these kinds of public-like spaces kind of crammed all together. We tried to fit as many of our favourite types of these kinds of transit public spaces. 

[b]N:[/b] There’s a lot of airport. 

[b]R:[/b] Yeah, airport as well. Those rail-like sky corridors that you walk in the main hub are straight up Umeda Sky Building. If you Google, you can see them. The foliage is very Hong Kong as opposed to North America. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/99596b4f75aad2667f9c247e17926d47babe80d2.jpg[/img]


[b]What are the unique challenges of designing a game that shifts so frequently between 3rd person adventure, visual novel and first-person walking sim?[/b]

[b]R:[/b] The writing had to shift a lot with each character and perspective, like the way we were delivering the story was very different. 

[b]N:[/b] Oh, for sure. Perhaps not so much in the dialogue, but you’re right. I don’t necessarily think that was challenging as much as it was treating every chapter as its own specimen, like its own ecosystem. It has its own tone and texture, that’s what I would say. Tell me about it from a design perspective. 

[b]R:[/b] From the beginning we wanted to lean in on what we were comfortable with and experienced in, and part of that was narrative, story, affect, and form, in lieu of traditional game mechanics. But it turns out that this is actually really hard because we just have to keep making unique content throughout the game. And that was a huge challenge. Like, every conversation is new, every event is new and unique. Every chapter is designed in a different way than the last one, or organized in a different way than the last one. Our main mechanic is time travelling, or time skipping, and we just had to keep finding ways to use it in different ways as well, to inform how we could tell the story. So it has felt like building three, four, five games instead of just one. Colin has done and is doing a really good job of keeping that all in check.


[b]If the Sunset Visitor team were given roles a la the Sisters of the game, what would your roles be?[/b]

[b]N:[/b] This would be my pick. You, Remy, would be of a Knower type–you kind of got that eldest sister poker face. You roll your eyes at the youngins, people with too much expression and not enough grit. And I would say that obviously, you know––

[b]R:[/b] You can stop there, yeah. 

N: Colin is a Fixing type. They’re pretty unfazed, really keen to figure out bugs, curious about why and how things work, and tries to make things better. A lot of the time we look to Colin, when troubleshooting, to lead our team. I think Kodai is an ALLMOTHER type. He has fire and youthful gusto. 

[b]R:[/b] He does sometimes say he has, what is it called? “Yellow demon spirit,” I think from Japanese folklore, like exactly what you’re saying. Funny enough, the ALLMOTHER’s colour is yellow. 

[b]N:[/b] Yeah, yeah like a poetic, brooding type. I think he’s got that heart as an artist. I think for me, [Producer] NT would be a great Principal. Like, always dressed immaculately, and really quite grounded, [she] has a thousand yard stare that could really beat you into submission, is really holding the fort, [and] can focus on what’s in front of her but can also see everything behind her. I would be of the Healing variety; a real big heart and weeping all the time, humanitarian inclinations, can read the room emotionally, and wants everyone to feel better. A big empath. So those would be my picks. How about you? 

[b]R:[/b] I agree with you. I agree with your picks. 

[b]N:[/b] Do you?

[b]R:[/b] I think it’s funny that we have nobody for Watcher and BBF. Those are the two that we don’t really have.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/cc12face8e54c2ca99c1ab153177498b4b58aa29.jpg[/img]


[b]What led to the decision to work with two composers? Was it a stylistic choice?[/b]

[b]R:[/b] There was just a lot of music required, and very early on it occurred to me we had to make the time shifting very clear–you know, you want visual feedback, you want some audio feedback as well. And it turned out it was great to also have some music feedback. So for every level or scene, we don’t have only one piece of music, we may have 5 or 10, or 12.

Something that I’ve always believed in, is that it’s very hard to sometimes just pretend yourself out of your own compositional voice. Having two compositional voices would allow for this difference to be felt, in a way that’s hard to describe. And for the composers, they can have a lot more fun, I think, to continually find different parts of their voice as opposed to us forcing them to use somebody else’s voice which is never good–you don’t always get good process out of that. 


[b]Anyone in particular you’d like to shout out from the voice/dialogue team?[/b]

[b]N:[/b] Natalie Tan, who has put in hundreds, thousands of hours of labour doing immaculate take selection. We have many, many, many characters, and––

[b]R:[/b] 15,000 lines. 

[b]N:[/b] 15,000 lines, and many of them hand crafted, and hand-cut, like Moodles by NT. And when you play the game, those voices make such a big difference in terms of amplifying affect and really making the story compelling. 

[b]R:[/b] If you calculate 15,000 chosen lines, then there’s at least like 100,000 takes that have probably been listened to at this point, and recorded.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/609707b4d17df2d52c6e40db885cbcf0eaffccf5.png[/img]


[b]What is your favourite feedback you've received to date about the game?[/b]

[b]N:[/b] When the demo was out, I remember the hashtag #justiceforjiao showed up on Twitch. Jiao is really near and dear to my heart and I spent a lot of time writing into her lived experience. So the fact that people got passionate about how she’s treated feels very rewarding. How about you? 

[b]R:[/b] We were on a top 10 of 2023 list on Giant Bomb, which is great because we haven’t released the game yet. But [the author] Meghna Jayanth said the game is a” lucid dream, handcrafted for you,” I think. I’m pretty happy about that. And there’s another person, Andrew Plotkin, who called it “compelling, overwhelming and agonizing.”

Project AWR (Asian Women Representation) are dedicated to the representation of Asian women, non-binary and marginalized identities in games.

Throughout the entire month, Project AWR will be highlighting Asian characters or Asian-led/Asian-focused games and giving a voice to some of the extraordinary Asian women who either developed these games, or voiced of our beloved characters, through a series of interviews.

In the first of this Asian Women in Games series, Project AWR interviews Jasmine Chen, Stephanie Wong, and Nhi Do—all based in Vancouver, British Columbia. They lend their voices to bring life to several characters in 1000XRESIST and we’re excited to explore the game and their experiences.

[h1]1000xRESIST[/h1]
Delve into a hyper-cinematic adventure with 1000xRESIST. 

You are Watcher, a clone who lives at the world's end. You worship the last surviving human: the ALLMOTHER. When a dangerous rumour shatters your faith, you phase through time and memory to expose a 1000-year-old lie. Relive. Reclaim. RESIST.

[h1]Join the cast as they play the debut demo[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/f70fe96cd68adbd1786562c1b2babe716db2e40f.png[/img]

Sunset Visitor invites you to join Nhi Do and Anjela Magpantay for the first public playthrough of their upcoming game, 1000xRESIST! Nhi and Anjela voice multiple characters in the game, with Nhi providing the dialogue for player character, Watcher!

[h1]Broadcast Restream[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42975267/e0d2cf0cf171e66bae45cf74f1109d3ca16f476a.gif[/img]

If you missed the stream, don't worry - it's pre-recorded and will be looped through the duration of Steam Next Fest on the game's page!

[h1]Download and play the demo now![/h1]
The demo will take you through the early hours of the game, giving you a taste of 1000xRESIST's striking atmosphere and unique style. You can expect around 90 minutes of gameplay, depending on how much you explore - and we DO recommend exploring as much of the school as possible. There's a lot of extra story, cool lore drops and general worldbuilding to be found!

Once you've finished playing, head over to the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1675830/discussions/0/3770111689908819324/]community hub[/url] and let us know your thoughts!
